candidates.title: VendIQ — vendor follow-up agent

ease.reason: The discovery title suggests vendor follow-ups, but no readable primary capabilities support a starter estimate.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: procurement teams could value follow-ups; neither a buyer nor demand is evidenced.

feasibility.reason: A narrow follow-up prototype is conceivable, but the supplied evidence cannot define its requirements.

autonomy.reason: The title implies follow-ups; no source establishes a repeatable loop or human review points.

evidence.reason: Only a discovery title is readable; robots validation blocked the selected primary page.

candidates.reason: Primary-page robots validation failed; the title alone cannot substantiate the product or a business loop.

candidates.title: OpenAI Dots orchestration concept

ease.reason: The article describes an orchestrating personal agent, but its tool integrations and underlying systems are inaccessible to a beginner clone.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: some professionals might pay for task orchestration; the article gives no demand evidence.

feasibility.reason: A narrow message-to-task prototype may fit two weeks, not the reported multi-chat cloud product.

autonomy.reason: The article describes proactive messages and delegated chats; users still connect tools and review results.

evidence.reason: A newsletter describes Dots and its plan availability; it is not primary product documentation or independent use evidence.

candidates.reason: This is an editorial report on another company’s broad assistant, not an assessable product lead with a supported small business loop.

candidates.title: Spotlight Off external-drive utility

ease.reason: The README documents a working macOS app and setup; a beginner still needs Swift and Full Disk Access knowledge.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: Mac users with external drives may pay for indexing control; no demand or revenue is established.

feasibility.reason: A limited drive-detection and indexing-status prototype is plausible in two weeks; signing and permissions complicate release.

autonomy.reason: The README describes detecting mounted drives and disabling indexing; setup, exceptions and permission recovery remain human tasks.

evidence.reason: The README describes features, installation, notarization and screenshots; customer use is not established.

candidates.reason: Working utility is documented, but the Mac permissions and release work constrain a beginner clone; its supported mean is below 6.

candidates.title: Invoice Agent Space

ease.reason: The selected Space yielded too little capability text to establish accessible tools or a beginner starting point.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: invoice processors may pay for extraction, but no product or buyer evidence is readable.

feasibility.reason: The supplied text cannot define an implementable two-week scope.

autonomy.reason: No readable evidence establishes an operating loop or human checks.

evidence.reason: Enrichment found too little readable product capability text; tags and title do not demonstrate a working system.

candidates.reason: The selected Space and enrichment did not provide readable product capabilities, so no meaningful product proposal is supportable.

candidates.title: Grep AI operations agents

ease.reason: YC’s page describes a managed platform with many integrations and skills; that breadth is not beginner-simple.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: businesses with repetitive operations may pay; the YC profile attributes customer and hours-saved claims to the company.

feasibility.reason: A high-stakes multi-domain agent platform is far beyond a useful two-week beginner version.

autonomy.reason: The page describes scheduled and monitored agents with dashboards; businesses still tune workflows and review high-stakes exceptions.

evidence.reason: The YC profile documents product mechanics and attributes named customer and usage claims to Grep; these are not independently verified here.

candidates.reason: The documented product spans high-stakes enterprise workflows; its small-business hypothesis is too broad for a two-week beginner build.

candidates.title: Invoice to Salesforce workflow

ease.reason: The template gives node-by-node instructions, but needs n8n, Google Drive, OCR, OpenAI and Salesforce credentials.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: firms handling invoices may pay for reduced entry work; this template shows no buyer demand.

feasibility.reason: A smaller test can process sample PDFs, but reliable accounting extraction and Salesforce mapping need careful setup.

autonomy.reason: A new-file trigger runs extraction and CRM writes; people must resolve parsing errors and verify financial records.

evidence.reason: The n8n page documents a detailed template and configuration, not a verified deployment or customer outcome.

candidates.reason: The documented integration chain is a useful example but depends on several credentials and financial-data checks; supported mean is below 6.

candidates.title: Dooza Desk support agent

ease.reason: The primary product page returned 404, leaving no readable setup or capability evidence.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small support teams might pay; the discovery title and failed page do not establish demand.

feasibility.reason: Without readable product requirements, a useful two-week version cannot be scoped from this evidence.

autonomy.reason: No accessible primary evidence establishes a repeatable support loop or human escalation points.

evidence.reason: Enrichment recorded HTTP 404; the discovery title is the only supplied product clue.

candidates.reason: The selected primary page returned 404, matching prior refusals for this same access limit; the title cannot support claims.

candidates.title: Lumro support and sales agents

ease.reason: The primary hostname did not resolve, so the supplied evidence cannot establish an accessible starting point.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: support or sales teams may pay for agents; no readable product or demand evidence supports it.

feasibility.reason: The title describes broad agent work without details to scope a useful two-week version.

autonomy.reason: No readable source establishes a recurring loop or human limits.

evidence.reason: Enrichment recorded DNS failure; only an unverified discovery title remains.

candidates.reason: The primary hostname did not resolve and the discovery title alone is insufficient, consistent with earlier refusals.

candidates.title: Pharmacy stock and expiry alerts

ease.reason: The n8n page gives a sheet layout and workflow steps; a beginner still needs Google and email credentials.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small pharmacies may value timely alerts; the template and testimonial do not establish willingness to pay.

feasibility.reason: A two-week prototype can check a sample sheet daily; pharmacy data quality and compliant operations need review.

autonomy.reason: The documented schedule reads stock and expiry fields, updates status and emails alerts; people maintain data and decide restocking.

evidence.reason: The template documents the flow and example sheet; its cited testimonial praises n8n generally, not this workflow’s outcomes.

candidates.reason: The template demonstrates a bounded alert loop, but demand is unproved and pharmacy data/setup limits a beginner business version.

candidates.title: Paganel verified database migration

ease.reason: The README describes a Rust migration engine and declarative pipeline language; database and systems experience are substantial prerequisites.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: teams may pay for safer migrations; the README gives no independent demand evidence.

feasibility.reason: Crash recovery, schema mapping and row-level verification exceed a useful beginner two-week build.

autonomy.reason: Configured migrations can run and verify automatically, but engineers must plan, approve and diagnose production changes.

evidence.reason: The README documents features and self-reported benchmark numbers; no independent deployment or customer evidence is supplied.

candidates.reason: The detailed README describes specialized database infrastructure, not a feasible beginner-sized product experiment.

candidates.title: Markdown review inside Azure DevOps

ease.reason: The README provides marketplace installation and a visual tour; building requires Azure DevOps extension knowledge.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: teams reviewing Markdown in pull requests may pay; no buyer or paid-demand evidence is shown.

feasibility.reason: A small rendered-Markdown viewer with anchored comments is plausible, though Azure integration and permissions add work.

autonomy.reason: The extension renders documents and diffs; reviewers still read content, judge changes and write comments.

evidence.reason: The README includes a showcase GIF, Marketplace install path and a founder statement that he built it for his own need.

candidates.reason: The working extension is credible evidence, but its central workflow is human review and no paid demand is established; mean is below 6.

candidates.title: SmartBI marketing data copilot

ease.reason: BetaList describes connecting common marketing sources, but a useful implementation needs multiple changing APIs.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small businesses may pay for marketing recommendations; the directory listing reports plans but not validated demand.

feasibility.reason: A two-week version could analyze one CSV source; reproducing live connectors and useful recommendations is broader.

autonomy.reason: The listing describes generated recommendations; a person connects accounts, explains business context and decides actions.

evidence.reason: The supplied BetaList page is directory copy with product description and plan claims, not a demo or verified usage.

candidates.reason: Only a directory listing supports this broad analytics idea; product behavior and real use are not independently demonstrated.
